questions.question: What is the distinction between representational harm and allocational harm in LLM deployments?
options: Representational harm is caused by the training data; allocational harm is caused by the model's inference
Representational harm involves biased portrayals of groups (stereotypes, erasure); allocational harm involves unequal material outcomes for groups (different resource distribution or recommendations)
Representational harm affects language models; allocational harm affects classification systems
Representational harm is measurable; allocational harm is theoretical
questions.explanation: Representational harms: stereotypes, erasure, demeaning portrayals (e.g., depicting nurses as exclusively female). Allocational harms: unequal material outcomes (e.g., scoring Black applicants' resumes lower). A model can be representationally unbiased while allocationally biased, so evaluations must measure both.

questions.question: Gallegos et al. (2024) categorize bias evaluation metrics into three types. Which of the following is the most ecologically valid?
options: Embedding-based metrics (WEAT-style co-occurrence tests)
Probability-based metrics (log-likelihood of stereotype-confirming completions)
Generated-text-based metrics (downstream task measurement on actual model outputs)
Activation-based metrics (MLP neuron correlation with identity terms)
questions.explanation: Generated-text-based metrics — measuring actual model behavior on downstream tasks like resume scoring or recommendation writing — are the most ecologically valid because they reflect real deployment consequences. Embedding-based metrics measure representations without capturing behavioral bias; probability-based metrics are one step closer but still indirect.

questions.question: An et al. (PNAS Nexus, 2025) measured intersectional bias in resume evaluation. What type of intersectional effect did they find?
options: Models showed no bias on single-axis evaluations but substantial bias on intersectional pairs
GPT-4o penalized Black women more than Black men and more than white women separately — an effect invisible to single-axis gender or race evaluation alone
Bias only appeared when the resume explicitly stated demographic information
All five tested models showed identical intersectional bias patterns
questions.explanation: An et al. found that GPT-4o penalized Black women on resume scoring more than Black men alone and more than white women alone — an intersectional amplification that single-axis (race-only or gender-only) bias evaluation would miss entirely. This is the key empirical case for intersectional evaluation.

questions.question: WinoIdentity (COLM 2025) introduces uncertainty-based fairness evaluation. What does it add that point-prediction evaluation misses?
options: It includes more demographic identity categories than previous fairness benchmarks

It measures whether the model's uncertainty over outcomes differs across intersectional identity tuples — catching cases where the model is equally wrong on average but more uncertain for some groups, producing different allocation behavior
It uses crowdsourced annotations to reduce labeler bias in fairness evaluation
It tests whether models can correctly identify their own biases when asked
questions.explanation: WinoIdentity measures uncertainty across intersectional identity tuples, not just mean accuracy. A model can show equal average error across groups while having higher variance for some groups — which downstream allocation systems will treat differently. Uncertainty-based evaluation catches this invisible form of differential treatment.

questions.question: Zhou et al.'s UniBias (2024) achieves zero-shot debiasing using which technique?
options: Suppressing specific MLP neurons identified as gender neurons
Reweighting or zeroing specific attention heads that amplify identity-class sensitivity, without requiring fine-tuning
Adding a bias penalty term to the decoding objective at inference time
Replacing identity terms in the prompt with demographically neutral alternatives
questions.explanation: UniBias (Zhou et al., ACL 2024) identifies specific attention heads that amplify sensitivity to identity-class features and reweights or zeros those heads at inference time. No fine-tuning is required — it is a zero-shot debiasing intervention at the attention mechanism level.

questions.question: The meta-critique (arXiv:2508.11067, 2025) identifies a systematic gap in the 10-year bias literature. What is it?
options: The literature focuses only on English-language models
The literature disproportionately focuses on binary-gender bias, neglecting disability, religion, migration status, multi-lingual identity, and other axes
The literature uses only embedding-based metrics, ignoring generated-text evaluation
The literature focuses only on generative models, neglecting classification models used in hiring and lending
questions.explanation: The 2025 meta-critique finds that the 10-year NLP bias literature is dominated by binary-gender bias. Other axes — disability, religion, migration status, multi-lingual identity — receive far less attention. The concern is that models well-debiased on the frequently-studied axes may remain badly biased on neglected dimensions.
